newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Intl Motor sees tough year in 97.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Intl Motor sees tough year in 97.

text.p: Jardine International Motor Holdings Ltd said it would do well this year to match 1996 results, with profit margins under pressure in Hong Kong and conditions tough in its major European market, France.
But a strong performance in Britain and continued strength in Hong Kong sales may help offset the difficulties, executives said after the company's annual general meeting on Wednesday.

"We will do well to match last year's results," chairman Anthony Nightingale said. Jardine International posted a 9.0 percent growth in profit after taxation but before exceptional items to US$68.90 million for calendar year 1996.
"We are seeing very good performance in the U.K. but it's been very tough in France," the chairman said.
Total car sales in France fell about 20 percent in most months in the first half of the year, he said.
Unit sales in France accounted for 54 percent of the company's total for the year ended December 31, 1996, according to its annual report.
In Hong Kong, total car sales rose 60 percent year on year in the first six months of 1997, said Richard Lee, a director at Jardine International.
Demand was set to be even higher in the second half after Hong Kong's July 1 change in sovereignty was settled, he said.
"Some delayed purchases decision will come up in the next six months and definitely it will benefit Mercedes-Benz as well," he said.

But demand for Mercedes-Benz cars outstripped supply from the German car maker and a change in product mix lowered profit margins, which would affect the contribution of Mercedes sales to the group, Nightingale said.
"The sales mix at the moment is different from what it was last year and that will affect its contribution," he said.
Sales of Mercedes-Benz cars surged about 20 percent in the first half of the year, but growth was lower than the whole market since Jardine could not get enough supply from Germany, Lee also said.
Jardine's wholly owned unit Zung Fu distributes Mercedes-Benz passenger and commercial vehicles in Hong Kong.
